examples: All three bilingual sentences are original fictional learning examples, not quotations from actual clinical reports and not medication, diagnosis or treatment instructions.
globalBoundaries: Allergy is a condition; allergic reaction names a reaction and can vary in severity. Neither is an unconditional anaphylaxis equivalent.
Anaphylaxis has serious systemic scope, but systemic does not mean every organ must visibly be involved. It is not a label for every local or general allergic symptom.
Anaphylactic shock is the shock-specific phrase; anaphylaxis can occur without circulatory shock. Do not equate these words unconditionally.
Allergen names a trigger/substance, not the reaction or the person. Generic poisoning and generic adverse effects are not automatically allergic reactions.

Only explicit complete positive Chinese aliases listed in source are proposed; exclusions below are semantic non-equivalences, not code to globally hide words. No global medical-adjective or source-family suppression.

entries.englishScope: Used of something connected with anaphylaxis, a serious systemic hypersensitivity reaction.
positiveChineseAliases: 严重全身性过敏反应的
entries.roleBoundary: An adjective can modify reaction or shock; it is not itself the generic noun allergic reaction. The Chinese ending的 deliberately preserves adjectival role.
entries.formBoundary: No inflection is proposed; current canonical forms are empty. No nominal plural or guessed family members.

entries.englishScope: Describes a presentation with features resembling those of anaphylaxis or anaphylactic shock.
entries.roleBoundary: Resemblance is essential; it does not identify every reaction as anaphylaxis or shock. The conventional类过敏反应的 label is explained with the specialized severe comparison, not used as generic过敏的.
entries.mechanismBoundary: No universal statement about IgE, immune/nonimmune mechanisms, mandatory diagnostic tests, current preferred terminology or historical obsolescence is proposed. Sources/terminology vary; only supported descriptive resemblance is admitted to this draft.
entries.formBoundary: No inflection or noun use is proposed; current canonical forms are empty.

entries.englishScope: A serious systemic hypersensitivity episode, usually beginning rapidly and capable of threatening life.
entries.roleBoundary: The complete serious/systemic context must be retained. The two shorter severe/systemic phrases are not declared unconditional equivalents on their own; every local or nonspecific allergy must not be reclassified through this noun.
entries.shockBoundary: The main definition is affirmative. The specialist source explicitly allows anaphylaxis without circulatory shock; the companion, not a false synonym alias, preserves that distinction.
entries.onsetBoundary: 通常 qualifies rapid onset; do not change it into always immediate, inevitably fatal, all-body visible symptoms or mandatory multi-organ involvement.
entries.countabilityBoundary: Cambridge marks uncountable; Oxford also allows countable use and plural anaphylaxes. This draft labels only noun and admits no new forms; it does not assert universal uncountable-only use or that anaphylaxes is invalid. Any additional form requires separate actual source-bound review.
